verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord spoke to Moses:
notes: The wilderness wandering officially having begun, these rules were then given for the people to be used when they finally entered the land. That they would be provided here would be of some encouragement to the nation after their great failure. God still spoke of a land that was to be their land, even though they had sinned greatly. This chapter collects a number of religious rules. The first 16 verses deal with rulings for sacrifices. Then, vv. 17-36 concerns sins of omission. Finally, rules concerning tassels are covered (vv. 37-41). For additional reading, see G. B. Gray, Sacrifice in the Old Testament (Oxford: Clarendon, 1925); B. A. Levine, In the Presence of the Lord (SJLA); D. J. McCarthy, “The Symbolism of Blood and Sacrifice,” JBL 88 (1969): 166-76; “Further Notes on the Symbolism of Blood and Sacrifice,” JBL 92 (1973): 205-10; J. Milgrom, “Sin Offering or Purification Offering,” VT 21 (1971): 237-39; N. H. Snaith, “Sacrifices in the Old Testament,” VT 7 (1957): 308-17; R. J. Thompson, Penitence and Sacrifice in Early Israel; R. de Vaux, Studies in Old Testament Sacrifice.

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：你们到了我所赐给你们居住的地，
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘When you enter the land where you are to live,[NOTE:1] which I am giving you,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the land of your habitations.”
The Hebrew participle here has the futur instans use of the participle, expressing that something is going to take place. It is not imminent, but it is certain that God would give the land to Israel.

verses.zh: 若愿意从牛群羊群中取牛羊作火祭，献给耶和华，无论是燔祭是平安祭，为要还特许的愿，或是作甘心祭，或是逢你们节期献的，都要奉给耶和华为馨香之祭。
verses.en: and you make an offering by fire to the Lord from the herd or from the flock (whether a burnt offering or a sacrifice for discharging a vow or as a freewill offering or in your solemn feasts) to create a pleasing aroma to the Lord,

verses.zh: 那献供物的就要将细面伊法十分之一，并油一欣四分之一，调和作素祭，献给耶和华。
verses.en: then the one who presents his offering to the Lord must bring[NOTE:1] a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of finely ground flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of olive oil.[NOTE:2]
notes: The three words at the beginning of this verse are all etymologically related: “the one who offers his offering shall offer.”

Obviously, as the wording of the text affirms, this kind of offering would be made after they were in the land and able to produce the grain and oil for the sacrifices. The instructions anticipated their ability to do this, and this would give hope to them. The amounts are difficult to determine, but it may be that they were to bring 4.5 liters of flour and 1.8 liters each of oil and wine.

verses.zh: 无论是燔祭是平安祭，你要为每只绵羊羔，一同预备奠祭的酒一欣四分之一。
verses.en: You must also prepare one-fourth of a hin of wine for a drink offering[NOTE:1] with the burnt offering or the sacrifice for each lamb.[NOTE:2]
notes: The drink-offering was an ancient custom, mentioned in the Ugaritic tablets of Ras Shamra (14th century b.c.). The drink offering was poured out at the base of the altar (see Sir 50:15 and Josephus, Ant. 3.9.4 [3.234]).
Heb “for the one lamb,” but it clearly means “for each lamb.”

verses.zh: 为公绵羊预备细面伊法十分之二，并油一欣三分之一，调和作素祭，
verses.en: Or for a ram, you must prepare as a grain offering two-tenths of an ephah of finely ground flour mixed with one-third of a hin of olive oil,

verses.zh: 又用酒一欣三分之一作奠祭，献给耶和华为馨香之祭。
verses.en: and for a drink offering you must offer one-third of a hin of wine as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

verses.zh: 你预备公牛作燔祭，或是作平安祭，为要还特许的愿，或是作平安祭，献给耶和华，
verses.en: And when you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice for discharging a vow or as a peace offering to the Lord,

verses.zh: 就要把细面伊法十分之三，并油半欣，调和作素祭，和公牛一同献上，
verses.en: then a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of finely ground flour mixed with half a hin of olive oil must be presented[NOTE:1] with the young bull,
notes: The text changes from direct address here to the third person form of the verb. If the MT is correct, then to make a smooth translation it would need to be made a passive (in view of the fact that no subject is expressed).

verses.zh: 又用酒半欣作奠祭，献给耶和华为馨香的火祭。
verses.en: and you must present as the drink offering half a hin of wine with the fire offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

verses.zh: 「献公牛、公绵羊、绵羊羔、山羊羔，每只都要这样办理。
verses.en: This is what is to be done[NOTE:1] for each ox, or each ram, or each of the male lambs or the goats.
notes: Heb “according to thus shall it be done.”

verses.zh: 照你们所预备的数目，按着只数都要这样办理。
verses.en: You must do so for each one according to the number that you prepare.

verses.zh: 凡本地人将馨香的火祭献给耶和华，都要这样办理。
verses.en: “‘Every native-born person must do these things in this way to present an offering made by fire as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

verses.zh: 若有外人和你们同居，或有人世世代代住在你们中间，愿意将馨香的火祭献给耶和华，你们怎样办理，他也要照样办理。
verses.en: If a resident foreigner is living[NOTE:1] with you—or whoever is among you[NOTE:2] in future generations[NOTE:3]—and prepares an offering made by fire as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, he must do it the same way you are to do it.[NOTE:4]
notes: The word גּוּר (gur) was traditionally translated “to sojourn,” i.e., to live temporarily in a land. Here the two words are from the root: “if a sojourner sojourns.”
Heb “in your midst.”
The Hebrew text just has “to your generations,” but it means in the future.
The imperfect tenses must reflect the responsibility to comply with the law, and so the classifications of instruction or obligation may be applied.

verses.zh: 至于会众，你们和同居的外人都归一例，作为你们世世代代永远的定例，在耶和华面前，你们怎样，寄居的也要怎样。
verses.en: One statute must apply[NOTE:1] to you who belong to the congregation and to the resident foreigner who is living among you, as a permanent[NOTE:2] statute for your future generations. You and the resident foreigner will be alike[NOTE:3] before the Lord.
notes: The word “apply” is supplied in the translation.
Or “a statute forever.”
Heb “as you, as [so] the alien.”

verses.zh: 你们并与你们同居的外人当有一样的条例，一样的典章。」
verses.en: One law and one custom must apply to you and to the resident foreigner who lives alongside you.’”

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：你们到了我所领你们进去的那地，
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘When you enter the land to which I am bringing you[NOTE:1]
notes: The relative clause is literally, “which I am causing you to enter there.” The final adverb is resumptive, and must be joined with the relative pronoun.

verses.zh: 吃那地的粮食，就要把举祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: and you eat[NOTE:1] some of the food of the land, you must offer up a raised offering[NOTE:2] to the Lord.
notes: The verse has a temporal clause that actually continues or supplements the temporal clause of the preceding verse. It is made up of the temporal indicator, the infinitive construct with the preposition, and the suffixed subjective genitive: “and it shall be when you eat.” Here it is translated simply “and eat” since the temporal element was introduced in the last verse.

This is the תְּרוּמָה (terumah), the “raised offering” or “heave offering” (cf. KJV, ASV). It may simply be called a “contribution” (so NAB). The verb of the sentence is from the same root: “you shall lift up/raise up.” It was to be an offering separated from the rest and raised up to the Lord in the sight of all. It was designed to remind the Israelites that the produce and the land belonged to God.

verses.zh: 你们要用初熟的麦子磨面，做饼当举祭奉献；你们举上，好像举禾场的举祭一样。
verses.en: You must offer up a cake of the first of your finely ground flour[NOTE:1] as a raised offering; as you offer the raised offering of the threshing floor, so you must offer it up.
notes: Or “the first of your dough.” The phrase is not very clear. N. H. Snaith thinks it means a batch of loaves from the kneading trough—the first batch of the baking (Leviticus and Numbers [NCB], 251).

verses.zh: 你们世世代代要用初熟的麦子磨面，当举祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: You must give to the Lord some of the first of your finely ground flour as a raised offering in your future generations.

verses.zh: 「你们有错误的时候，不守耶和华所晓谕摩西的这一切命令，
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “‘If you[NOTE:2] sin unintentionally and do not observe all these commandments that the Lord has spoken to Moses—
notes: These regulations supplement what was already ruled on in the Levitical code for the purification and reparation offerings. See those rulings in Lev 4-7 for all the details. Some biblical scholars view the rules in Leviticus as more elaborate and therefore later. However, this probably represents a misunderstanding of the purpose of each collection.
The verb is the plural imperfect; the sin discussed here is a sin committed by the community, or the larger part of the community.

verses.zh: 就是耶和华藉摩西一切所吩咐你们的，自那日以至你们的世世代代，
verses.en: all that the Lord has commanded you by the authority[NOTE:1] of Moses, from the day that the Lord commanded Moses and continuing through your future generations—
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 若有误行，是会众所不知道的，后来全会众就要将一只公牛犊作燔祭，并照典章把素祭和奠祭一同献给耶和华为馨香之祭，又献一只公山羊作赎罪祭。
verses.en: then if anything is done unintentionally[NOTE:1] without the knowledge of[NOTE:2] the community, the whole community must prepare one young bull for a burnt offering—for a pleasing aroma to the Lord—along with its grain offering and its customary drink offering, and one male goat for a purification offering.
notes: The idea of לִשְׁגָגָה (lishgagah) seems to be that of “inadvertence” or “without intent.” The text gives no indication of how this offense might be committed, or what it might include. It probably describes any transgressions done in ignorance of the Law that involved a violation of tabernacle procedure or priestly protocol or social misdemeanor. Even though it was done unintentionally, it was still a violation and called for ritual purification.
Heb “[away] from the eyes of the community.”

verses.zh: 祭司要为以色列全会众赎罪，他们就必蒙赦免，因为这是错误。他们又因自己的错误，把供物，就是向耶和华献的火祭和赎罪祭，一并奉到耶和华面前。
verses.en: And the priest is to make atonement[NOTE:1] for the whole community of the Israelites, and they will be forgiven, because it was unintentional and they have brought their offering, an offering made by fire to the Lord, and their purification offering before the Lord, for their unintentional offense.
notes: The verb is the Piel perfect with vav (ו) consecutive (וְכִפֶּר, vekhipper) to continue the instruction of the passage: “the priest shall make atonement,” meaning the priest is to make atonement for the sin (thus the present translation). This verb means “to expiate,” “to atone for,” “to pacify.” It describes the ritual events by which someone who was separated from the holy Lord God could find acceptance into his presence through the sacrificial blood of the substitutionary animal. See Lev 1 and Num 16:41-50.

verses.zh: 以色列全会众和寄居在他们中间的外人就必蒙赦免，因为这罪是百姓误犯的。
verses.en: And the whole community[NOTE:1] of the Israelites and the resident foreigner who lives among them will be forgiven, since all the people were involved in the unintentional offense.
notes: Again, rather than translate literally “and it shall be forgiven [to] them” (all the community), one could say, “they (all the community) will be forgiven.” The meaning is the same.

verses.zh: 「若有一个人误犯了罪，他就要献一岁的母山羊作赎罪祭。
verses.en: “‘If any person[NOTE:1] sins unintentionally, then he must bring a yearling female goat for a purification offering.
notes: The Hebrew text has וְאִם־נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת (veʾim nefesh ʾakhat), sometime translated “and if any soul.” But the word describes the whole person, the soul in the body; it refers here to the individual who sins.

verses.zh: 那误行的人犯罪的时候，祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪，他就必蒙赦免。
verses.en: And the priest must make atonement for the person who sins unintentionally—when he sins unintentionally before the Lord—to make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.

verses.zh: 以色列中的本地人和寄居在他们中间的外人，若误行了甚么事，必归一样的条例。
verses.en: You must have one law for the person who sins unintentionally, both for the native-born among the Israelites and for the resident foreigner who lives among them.

verses.zh: 但那擅敢行事的，无论是本地人是寄居的，他亵渎了耶和华，必从民中剪除。
verses.en: “‘But the person[NOTE:1] who acts defiantly,[NOTE:2] whether native-born or a resident foreigner, insults[NOTE:3] the Lord.[NOTE:4] That person[NOTE:5] must be cut off[NOTE:6] from among his people.
notes: Heb “soul.”

The sin is described literally as acting “with a high hand”—בְּיָד רָמָה (beyad ramah). The expression means that someone would do something with deliberate defiance, with an arrogance in spite of what the Lord said. It is as if the sinner was about to attack God, or at least lifting his hand against God. The implication of the expression is that it was done in full knowledge of the Law (especially since this contrasts throughout with the sins of ignorance). Blatant defiance of the word of the Lord is dealt with differently. For similar expressions, see Exod 14:8 and Num 33:3.
The verb occurs only in the Piel; it means “to blaspheme,” “to revile.”
The word order in the Hebrew text places “Yahweh” first for emphasis—it is the Lord such a person insults.
Heb “soul.”

The clause begins with “and” because the verb is the perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive. As discussed with Num 9:13, to be cut off could mean excommunication from the community, death by the community, or death by divine intervention.

verses.zh: 因他藐视耶和华的言语，违背耶和华的命令，那人总要剪除；他的罪孽要归到他身上。」
verses.en: Because he has despised[NOTE:1] the Lord’s message and has broken[NOTE:2] his commandment, that person[NOTE:3] must be completely cut off.[NOTE:4] His iniquity will be on him.’”[NOTE:5]
notes: The verb בָּזָה (bazah, “to despise”) means to treat something as worthless, to treat it with contempt, to look down the nose at something as it were.
The verb פָּרַר (parar, “to break”) can mean to nullify, break, or violate a covenant.
Heb “soul.”

The construction uses the Niphal imperfect with the modifying Niphal infinitive absolute. The infinitive makes the sentence more emphatic. If the imperfect tense is taken as an instruction imperfect, then the infinitive makes the instruction more binding. If it is a simple future, then the future is certain. In either case, there is no exclusion from being cut off.
The point is that the person’s iniquity remains with him—he must pay for his sin. The judgment of God in such a case is both appropriate and unavoidable.

verses.zh: 以色列人在旷野的时候，遇见一个人在安息日捡柴。
verses.en: When the Israelites were[NOTE:1] in the wilderness they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.[NOTE:2]
notes: The preterite of the verb “to be” is here subordinated to the next, parallel verb form, to form a temporal clause.

For this brief passage, see A. Phillips, “The Case of the Woodgatherer Reconsidered,” VT 19 (1969): 125-28; J. Weingreen, “The Case of the Woodgatherer (Numbers XV 32-36),” VT 16 (1966): 361-64; and B. J. Bamberger, “Revelations of Torah after Sinai,” HUCA 16 (1941): 97-113. Weingreen argues that there is something of the Rabbinic method of setting a fence around the Law here; in other words, if this sin were not punished, the Law would have been violated in greater ways. Gathering of wood, although seemingly harmless, is done with intent to kindle fire, and so reveals a culpable intent.

verses.zh: 遇见他捡柴的人，就把他带到摩西、亚伦并全会众那里，
verses.en: Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and to the whole community.

verses.zh: 将他收在监内；因为当怎样办他，还没有指明。
verses.en: They put him in custody, because there was no clear instruction about what should be done to him.

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐摩西说：「总要把那人治死；全会众要在营外用石头把他打死。」
verses.en: Then the Lord said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death; the whole community must stone[NOTE:1] him with stones outside the camp.”
notes: The sentence begins with the emphatic use of the infinitive absolute with the verb in the Hophal imperfect: “he shall surely be put to death.” Then, a second infinitive absolute רָגוֹם (ragom) provides the explanatory activity—all the community is to stone him with stones. The punishment is consistent with other decrees from God (see Exod 31:14, 15; 35:2). Moses had either forgotten such, or they had simply neglected to (or were hesitant to) enact them.

verses.zh: 于是全会众将他带到营外，用石头打死他，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。
verses.en: So the whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him to death,[NOTE:1] just as the Lord commanded Moses.
notes: Heb “stoned him with stones, and he died.”

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你吩咐以色列人，叫他们世世代代在衣服边上做繸子，又在底边的繸子上钉一根蓝细带子。
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make[NOTE:1] tassels[NOTE:2] for themselves on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and put a blue thread[NOTE:3] on the tassel of the corners.
notes: The construction uses the imperative followed by perfect tenses with vav (ו) consecutives. The first perfect tense may be translated as the imperative, but the second, being a third common plural form, has to be subordinated as a purpose clause, or as the object of the preceding verb: “speak…and say…that they make.”

This is a reference to the צִיצִת (tsitsit), the fringes on the borders of the robes. They were meant to hang from the corners of the upper garment (Deut 22:12), which was worn on top of the clothing. The tassel was probably made by twisting the overhanging threads of the garment into a knot that would hang down. This was a reminder of the covenant. The tassels were retained down through history, and today more elaborate prayer shawls with tassels are worn during prayer. For more information, see F. J. Stephens, “The Ancient Significance of Sisith,” JBL 50 (1931): 59-70; and S. Bertman, “Tasselled Garments in the Ancient East Mediterranean,” BA 24 (1961): 119-28.
The blue color may represent the heavenly origin of the Law, or perhaps, since it is a royal color, the majesty of the Lord.

verses.zh: 你们佩带这繸子，好叫你们看见就记念遵行耶和华一切的命令，不随从自己的心意、眼目行邪淫，像你们素常一样；
verses.en: You must have this tassel so that you may look at it and remember all the commandments of the Lord and obey them and so that you do not follow[NOTE:1] after your own heart and your own eyes that lead you to unfaithfulness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “seek out, look into.”

This last clause is a relative clause explaining the influence of the human heart and physical sight. It literally says, “which you go whoring after them.” The verb for “whoring” may be interpreted to mean “act unfaithfully.” So, the idea is these influences lead to unfaithful activity: “after which you act unfaithfully.”

verses.zh: 使你们记念遵行我一切的命令，成为圣洁，归与你们的　神。
verses.en: Thus[NOTE:1] you will remember and obey all my commandments and be holy to your God.
notes: This clause also serves as a purpose/result clause of the preceding—“in order that you may remember….” But because the line is so long, it is simpler to make this a separate sentence in the translation.

verses.zh: 「我是耶和华―你们的　神，曾把你们从埃及地领出来，要作你们的　神。我是耶和华―你们的　神。」
verses.en: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.”

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.

This VERB (BDB 154, KB 180, always in Piel stem) means to impugn one's character
by acting in certain ways (cf. 2 Kgs. 19:22; Isa. 37:23; Ezek. 10:27, NIDOTTE, vol, 1, pp. 828-830). YHWH is blasphemed
when His people act in knowingly rebellious ways. It is not just their words but their acts that reveal their hearts (Num. 15:31)!

In the NT "YHWH" comes before the VERB for emphasis. The consequences for speaking
against YHWH are spelled out in Lev. 24:15-16.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why do these laws about sacrifice break into the narrative at this point?

- Define "unintentional sin."

- What was the purpose of tassels?

- How does Num. 15:40 relate to Lev. 11:44; 19:2?
